title: Tironian teaching pairs as a self-defining key for complete word and clause notation
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. A historical shorthand dictionary supplies both the actual compound sign and its literal Latin expansion, including attested multiword clauses. A single global recoding of graphical primitives must explain BOTH representations in every complete teaching record; after that key is identified, the same fixed sign lexicon can decode complete ordinary shorthand passages. This is a source-grounded candidate, not a claim that Voynich contains such paired records. No target was opened or fitted.

design.mechanism: Freeze a finite external catalogue D of complete pairs (G_e,L_e), where G_e is the whole attested Tironian note graph and L_e is its complete attested Latin word sequence, with original entry and variant provenance. Freeze the ordinary written-letter graphs used to spell L_e in the same source witness. A complete teaching record has the two fields NOTE(G_e) and SPELL(L_e), in an independently established fixed order. Both fields pass through ONE global injective relabeling gamma of a finite graphical primitive alphabet, preserving every incidence, cyclic attachment order and explicitly observed disconnection. Gamma maps primitive types to primitive types, never whole note IDs to chosen meanings; it cannot add/delete strokes, alter field order, insert padding or use note-specific values. The historical source attests sign/expansion pairs; this shared recoding is an explicit new hypothesis, not an attested Tironian cipher.
design.unit: Every record of a separately admitted complete paired-record domain must be consumed as one entire source pair; every written group and every stroke is accounted for. Source entries may repeat unless the particular historical witness independently requires otherwise. The initial domain may not be a selected set of good matches. Once gamma is fixed, a complete prose passage is a concatenation of complete source-attested notes whose fixed expansions are concatenated in order. All whole-note readings, including genuine source homographs and variant expansions, remain alternatives. Incomplete stem glosses, unreadable signs and undocumented productive attachments are not silently expanded. The contract therefore has an explicit finite source-vocabulary ceiling.
design.source_representation: Source and target primitive graphs must be observed independently before key search. A possible representation cuts visible ink at endpoints, junctions and corners and records the resulting primitive types and ordered attachment ports. Ductus not visible in a still image must not be invented; bounded observation alternatives remain alternatives. The exact primitive catalogue and paired-record geometry are presently UNFROZEN. If they cannot be defined independently and reproducibly, do not build the decoder. The lexicon navigation tree is not itself the writing grammar: Hellmann explicitly warns that a lookup-head meaning generally does not supply the meaning of the compound note.
design.independent_binding: The duplicated content is represented by two different source objects: a compact shorthand sign and the literal spelling of its expansion. Shared primitive values across both sides couple the note lexicon to Latin spelling, rather than allowing a permutation of opaque word IDs. Complete attested clause notes exist: CNT61,2 expands to ut uobis superius dixi; CNT61,3 to ut uobis inferius dixi; CNT49,51 to nihil enim est. These expansions are source data, not target-fitted phrase templates. They do not justify assigning above/below to an isolated graphical component.
design.identifiability: A successful fit must retain every global gamma, source-entry assignment and observation alternative. Automorphisms of the joint paired codebook can still permute entries, and unobserved primitives remain unidentified. Only expansions identical in every surviving model are decoded. If the same model merely maps each whole target note to a free catalogue entry, it collapses to an arbitrary dictionary and fails this design. GDT888-style unlabeled semantic incidence matching is not the constraint here: the immutable source side includes literal complete note graphs AND their spelled expansions.
design.prediction: A decisive prospective case requires a physically delimited new complete paired passage, with note fields and expansion fields identifiable without reading their values. Freeze gamma and all source ambiguities using the admitted discovery material. Reveal only the new note fields and predict every corresponding complete expansion field through the fixed source dictionary and the same gamma before those fields are read. No new primitive value, entry-specific spelling, changed record cut or residual omission is permitted. A contradiction rejects the complete paired-code law; unresolved predictions do not count as recovered meaning. Only after this transfer may the same unchanged key be applied to complete unpaired shorthand prose. No such target paired-record endpoint has been established.
design.source: Martin Hellmann, Supertextus Notarum Tironianarum: https://martinellus.de/snt2/n/basis.htm ; https://martinellus.de/snt2/n/admoniti.htm ; https://martinellus.de/snt2/n/structur.htm . Actual complete clause cards and original entry IDs: https://martinellus.de/snt2/notae/abduxit.htm . The author reports approximately13000 of an estimated15000 CNT notes entered, with the syllable/ending inventory complete and two bounded witness vocabularies complete (Voss.lat.O15, approximately200 word notes; Vat.Pal.lat.1710, approximately500). This is NOT a complete digital transcription of all CNT notes. Schmitz1893 original edition is available from the Boston Public Library digitization https://archive.org/details/commentariinotar00schm ; its metadata lists394 images and132 plates. Actual complete page and variant coverage still requires source-only collation. A native paired teaching-dictionary witness is Geneva, Bibliotheque de Geneve, Ms.lat.85, described by its holding library through e-codices: https://www.e-codices.ch/en/list/one/bge/lat0085 ; metadata mirror https://iiif.biblissima.fr/collections/manifest/1cd8cd569e0e53c77f66f0978a28aff31cff1d8e . No manuscript page was opened in this proposal pass.
design.contrast: Primary predecessors checked: GDT207 rejects its direct diplomatic letter-map screen and asks for an external constrained unit/parallel key; GDT288 has opaque payload and contextual renderer slots; GDT298 explicitly retains a high-capacity joint form lexicon without meanings; GDT609 proposes a technical34-slot abbreviation regularizer, not a historically fixed34-sign codebook. None of those reports supplies this actual sign-plus-spelled-expansion lexicon. IDEA000123 uses first letters of complete clauses; the proposed note expansions here are historical table entries with full graphical forms. IP058 is a related raw fixed-learning-pair idea, but its lexical match is not a novelty adjudication. The proposed source binding is distinct from the Latin CV and Alberti complete-entry channels of895/896; it does not reopen either failure or substitute a new corpus into those decoders.
design.scope: Raw source/architecture lead only. Missing: independently measured primitive inventories, a complete source freeze, a target paired-record domain, and an identified transferable key. No experiment, target transcript, new Voynich page, named-plant lookup, source-selection fit or meaning claim occurred. Bounded memory/duplicate searches are navigation, not proof of originality. Retain only for source/design review; no decoder construction is authorized by this card alone.
